([[Middletown, Delaware]]) | college = [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] (2014–2016) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * First-team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] (2016) * Big East Most Improved Player (2016) }} '''Benjamin Bentil''' (born March 29, 1995) is an Ghanaian [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career at [[Providence College]], declaring his eligibility for the [[NBA draft]] following his [[sophomore]] season. Bentil and his family moved from Ghana to the United States when he was 15 and Bentil's athletic prowess earned him a scholarship to [[St. Andrew's School (Delaware)|St. Andrew's School]] in [[Middletown, Delaware]]. He played for the school's [[soccer]] and basketball teams, ultimately earning a basketball scholarship at Providence.{{cite web | last = Forgrave | first = Reid | title = Far from Ghana, Providence's Ben Bentil has found a home | work = FoxSports.com | date = February 9, 2016 | url = http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/providence-friars-ben-bentil-ghana-family-big-east-basketball-020916 | accessdate = May 31, 2016}} After playing sparingly in his freshman season, the 6'9 [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] had a breakout season as a sophomore in 2015–16. He led the [[Big East Conference]] in scoring at 21.1 [[points per game]] and added 7.7 [[rebounds per game]]. At the close of the season, Bentil was named first-team All-Big East and the conference's most improved player.{{cite web | last = McNamara | first = Kevin | title = Big East names Kris Dunn Defensive Player of Year, Ben Bentil Most Improved | work = [[Providence Journal]] | date = March 7, 2016 | url = http://www.providencejournal.com/article/20160307/sports/160309462 | accessdate = May 31, 2016}} Following the conclusion of his sophomore season, Bentil declared himself eligible for the [[2016 NBA draft]]. After taking part in the NBA combine and gauging his stock with NBA teams, Bentil signed with an agent, ending his college career.{{cite web | last = Blakeley | first = A. Sherrod | title = Ben Bentil ready for opportunity to showcase his talents in the NBA | work = CSNNE.com | date = May 24, 2016 | url = http://www.csnne.com/2016-NBA-Draft-Ben-Bentil-ready-showcase-talents-providence-friars | accessdate = May 31, 2016}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.friars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ben_bentil_912651.html Providence Friars bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Bentil, Ben}} [[Category:1995 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Ghanaian basketball players]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Providence Friars men's basketball players]]
